decisions: Keep compiler defaults unchanged: small FP32 block levels 0/1/2 do not show a clear latency gain; trace replay needs full-flow confirmation.
Keep LoRA merging opt-in: single 512-token pretrained comparison is about 3% faster, with additional numerical drift.
Prioritize profiling: full shape generated IR uses 60 standalone softmax operations and no fused SDPA. Measure before assigning bottleneck percentages.
Full 512-token profile: matmuls are 6.16% of kernel-duration sums; complex RoPE pair tiling is the main identified avoidable cost.

Opt-in real-pair RoPE is 3.56x faster for the complete pretrained 512-token shape flow, bitwise equal on FP32 CPU, slightly lower device error and no reported fallback. Keep production default unchanged pending larger shapes, trajectories and scene quality.
Whole-flow level 1 retains fused SDPA but gains only 4.4% at 512 tokens and raises relative error from 6.8% to 9.3%. Do not change the default.

Matched PJRT 6181-token shape forwards: stock 23.5107s vs real-pair RoPE 6.6228s (3.55x), no reported fallback. Texture 512-token real-pair forward is 0.6287s, without a matched stock texture timing in that experiment.

Original 12-step 512-token shape sampler is 46.86s stock vs 13.24s real-pair RoPE (3.54x), but both fail trajectory smoke: final relative L2 0.411/0.383 vs identical FP32 CPU. Candidate vs stock TT relative L2 is 0.323. Do not claim quality preservation or promote.

CPU diagnostic with BF16 boundaries and FP32 products yields 0.239 final relative L2 vs FP32, but TT vs diagnostic remains about 0.39. Precision differences alone do not explain the TT discrepancy; diagnostic is not a CUDA oracle.

Optimized generated profile on the same alternate Metal SDK reduces kernel sums 2172.7ms to 603.6ms; matrix products stay 133.8/134.0ms. Explicit index-dtype compatibility repair was needed and recorded. Reshape is now largest at 192.3ms.
HiFi3 fidelity trial worsens final relative L2 to 0.422 with no recompilation/fallback; reject as accuracy fix, retain default HiFi4.

Poster image/camera hashes, original crop and occupancy decoder are restored. New finite conditioning [1,8,1029,1024] and independently seeded occupancy inputs are prepared. Projection and learned aggregation use FP32 CPU to isolate sampler errors from upstream TT drift.

Matched native sparse 6181-token control fails on exact 607617024-byte allocation; real-pair RoPE alone passes at 7.860s with zero FP32 CPU preparation drift and no reported fallback. Failure is contiguous DRAM-bank fragmentation despite adequate aggregate free space. Full native trajectory quality remains untested.

Full stock 6181-token generated profile is complete after increasing program capacity to 10000 and reading profiler buffers between forwards outside timing. 4973 measured device ops, 23.58s kernel sum, 9.68% matmul and 2.38% standalone softmax. Padded complex-pair layouts still dominate; these are kernel sums, not module wall attribution. Default-buffer overflow capture rejected and retained.

Authorized direct Facebook DINO source is restored after user HF login. Weights match the historical SHA256; all effective config fields match the public conversion, and all eight cropped poster features/cameras are bitwise equal to the prepared real-image sampler fixture.

Generated-code timing labels were corrected: activation loader uploads before the forward window. New explicit preload synchronization and separate preparation timing are hardware-validated with bitwise unchanged output. Historical raw reports remain intact with a linked scope correction; separate PJRT timings include fresh transfers.

Full occupancy candidate profile: 4096 tokens, 30 blocks, 4406 measured device ops, 3.97s kernel sum. Reshape is 29.8%, matmul 25.1%, binary 16.7%. This alternate SDK profile is not module wall-time attribution or quality evidence.

All 32 captured shape states preserve exact ordinary TT final output and repeat exactly. First block already has about 2% error, nonmonotonic over depth; final hidden error 1.97% vs prediction 6.69%. Isolate first-block suboperations and output head rather than assuming monotonic accumulation.

Completed real-poster occupancy sampler: stock 364.935s vs real-pair 88.121s, 4.141x over the same 12 steps and 22 forwards. Both fail FP32 trajectory gates at about 74.8% relative L2; candidate-vs-stock TT is 29.4%. No fallback or trajectory recompilation. No quality-preserving promotion.

Common FP32 CPU occupancy decoder isolates sampler effects: 6464 occupied reference voxels, 4163 stock TT, 4241 candidate. Stock/candidate IoU vs FP32 is 0.509/0.514; TT variants IoU is 0.913. One-crop topology changes prevent preserved-quality claims; this is not mesh/CUDA equivalence.

Both independently computed real-image stock FP32 CPU references are bitwise equal. Sealed cache retains original model/reference source and exact fixture identity; physical checkpoint bytes are rescanned on reuse. Full validation 2.52s vs original 743s CPU trajectory. Initial 70ms tensor/manifest-only validation excluded checkpoint rescan.

Validation passed: preceding 89-test CPU regression suite plus 2 subtests; 10 cache and 4 sampler checks; 3 occupancy-metric checks; 9 precision/input checks. Hardware numerical diagnostics retain failed quality gates explicitly.

Real-poster CPU pipeline precision calibration completed: latent relative L2 0.415 vs FP32 but common-decoder occupancy IoU 0.868. Both TT variants still differ about 0.71 from this diagnostic, with occupancy IoU about 0.54. Intended BF16 boundaries alone do not explain the device gap.

Reject codegen/inference interleaving: codegen_py changes process-global backend options and mutates exported modules. Controlled isolated attention outputs match a separate no-export process bitwise; actual native IR can instead be dumped using export_path and dry_run=false.

On identical learned first-block Q/K/V, FP32 postscale attention reduces self-attention error from 0.102 to 0.0272; cross-attention remains about 0.0182. Stage capture matches ordinary final output bitwise. Local QK error is below 0.0006, scale is exact, and native softmax error is 0.0399 self / 0.0236 cross on identical TT scores.

Stable exp times reciprocal(sum(exp)) avoids the compiler DivOp softmax fusion and reduces local softmax error to 0.000631 self / 0.000255 cross, with exact repeats and no fallback. Direct exp/div fuses back to native softmax. Approximate-exp defaults in exact SDK sources are a hypothesis, not a toggle-tested causal finding. exp2 was rejected for CPU fallback.

An initial full-flow attention run prepared only 30 cross-attention modules because top-level and package imports created different RoPE wrapper classes. Retain it as a partial-attention control, not the complete candidate. Canonical package imports and fail-closed unknown-wrapper checks prevent silent partial preparation.

Cross-only 30-module reciprocal control completed: 14.35s trajectory, final relative L2 0.435 vs original FP32 and 0.416 vs matched CPU precision diagnostic, no fallback or recompile. It does not improve trajectory agreement. Native IR retains 30 BF16 softmax and replaces only 30 cross softmax. Complete 60-module experiment remains separate.

Local softmax accuracy improvement does not resolve complete sampler drift: final relative L2 0.392 vs original FP32, 0.400 vs matched CPU precision diagnostic. Single-forward error is 0.0562. No promotion. Matched control subsequently completed; see result039.

Candidate reduces single-forward relative L2 from 0.06691 to 0.05618 but final sampler error increases from 0.38258 to 0.39210 and costs about 13–14% more time. Native local softmax gains are insufficient to improve this trajectory.

Real-poster latent error decreases from 0.7488 to 0.6074 vs FP32 and from 0.7174 to 0.5472 vs the CPU precision diagnostic. This costs 129.73s vs 88.12s for the original 22-forward sampler (47.2% longer). Single-forward error is 0.03324. Numerical gates remain failed; the process returncode 1 records those gates, not a native runtime crash.

Under the same original FP32 CPU decoder and zero threshold, real-poster occupied-grid IoU vs FP32 improves from 0.5135 with real-RoPE SDPA to 0.6776 with FP32 reciprocal attention; occupied voxels rise from 4241 to 5690 vs reference 6464. IoU vs CPU precision diagnostic improves from 0.5361 to 0.7227. CPU precision diagnostic vs FP32 remains 0.8684. Controls decode bitwise identically to retained historical grids.

BF16 AV preserves isolated accuracy: self error 0.01290 to 0.01293, cross 0.00644 to 0.00618. Isolated measured times fall about 13% self and 3% cross vs the extracted FP32 baseline, but these millisecond operator timings do not predict full-flow speed. BF16 QK raises self error to 0.0999; its CPU quantization diagnostic already incurs 0.1014, so keep QK FP32 for the next full-flow candidate.

For accepted full shape captures, CPU execution of the original head on actual TT hidden values has 6.77% error vs the stock prediction; observed TT prediction error is 6.69%. Combined native head arithmetic differs only 0.522% from CPU on identical TT hidden values. Hidden error is 1.97%, normalized-hidden error 1.71%. The learned projection amplifies upstream differences; a separate output-head precision fix is low priority on this fixture. These metrics are not additive error components.

Every refreshed TT sampler state and final sample matches the legacy FP32 reciprocal run bitwise. Sampler time 129.725s matches prior129.726s closely. Extracting shared arithmetic did not alter this full-model execution. Strict reference gates still fail at final relative L2 0.6074; this control is not a promotion.

BF16 AV decreases real-poster final latent error vs stock FP32 from 0.6074 to 0.5750. Forward latency is 5824.9ms vs 5886.1ms; complete sampler timings are retained below. This is an exploratory matched run on one crop, not proof of general accuracy or a statistically established small speed gain.

Real-poster BF16 AV improves occupancy IoU vs the same FP32 reference from 0.6776 to 0.7132, with 5660 occupied voxels vs 6464 reference. False positives/negatives fall from 781/1555 to 613/1417. Sampler time is 128.155s vs 129.725s in the paired run (1.21% lower). All legacy/refreshed reference control grids decode bitwise identically.

Source-level head-first views do not realize the intended device layout. Native IR retains 60 RoPE multiplies with token-first phase shapes and padded 12-head rows, with60 extra typecasts vs control. The candidate is slower (650.0ms vs625.7ms per forward, 13.63s vs13.21s sampler) and differs 30.6% from TT control at final state despite exact CPU preparation.

Explicit contiguous head-first inputs still leave the cosine multiply token-first in native IR, with native output bitwise equal to token-first. Flattening head/token rows changes the native cosine multiply to [1,12,T,128] with [1,1,T,128] phases. On seeded BF16 inputs, flat output matches CPU bitwise at both512 and4096 tokens; baseline relative L2 is about0.00055/0.00065. At4096, measured kernel+output-transfer median falls28.06ms to12.60ms (2.23x); at512 it increases4.17ms to4.44ms. These are kernel results, not full-flow measurements.

Flattened head-first and token-first formulations both match CPU bitwise on the seeded BF16 fixtures. At4096, head-first prototype median13.15ms vs token-first16.39ms; integrated head-first12.18ms and bitwise equal to prototype. All eight preintegration native outputs match the independent integration process bitwise. Baseline microtiming varies between processes (about26.6–36.2ms at4096), so do not treat precise kernel ratios or small512-token differences as full-flow performance evidence.

Flattened head-first RoPE reduces the complete poster sampler from128.155s to104.503s (1.226x,18.46% lower), with forward median5824.9ms to4755.1ms. Final relative L2 vs stock FP32 is0.5726 vs0.5750. Native IR realizes60 head-first cosine multiplies; nominal cosine-result payload is24MiB vs64MiB and phase payload2MiB vs64MiB, excluding allocator overhead. Other layout/gather operations also change, so this does not attribute all saved time to one operator.

On the same poster crop and original FP32 decoder, flattened head-first RoPE raises occupancy IoU vs stock FP32 from0.7132 to0.7274 while reducing sampler time128.155s to104.503s. Occupied count5821 vs reference6464; false positives648 vs613 control, false negatives1291 vs1417 control. All five historical control grids remain bitwise unchanged.

FP32 model tensors reduce final relative error from0.3921 to0.2936 while increasing sampler time from about15.01s to18.89s. Parameter payload grows2.723GB to5.377GB and fits this device. All457 native-IR linear/matmul operations use FP32 operands, but60 RoPE embeddings still use BF16 tables introduced by lowering. Promoting model tensors alone does not preserve FP32 through every primitive and does not resolve trajectory drift.

Prepared CPU final relative L2 vs stock is0.00010576 (0.0106%) and every original state passes existing gates. TT differs0.29359 from the same prepared CPU trajectory.114 critical model/reference/helper source hashes match native run068, and physical checkpoint hash is verified. The large native drift is not explained by the small helper algebra difference observed on CPU.

Native flattened FP32 RoPE output equals a CPU counterfactual rounding only the gathered partner to BF16 bitwise at both 512 and 4096 tokens. Native IR explicitly casts the lookup table to BF16 and the result back to FP32. Relative L2 is about0.000588/0.000675. This proves a local lookup loss on these seeded inputs, not its contribution to complete sampler error.

Simple three-payload FP32-to-BF16 residual splitting fails on hardware: final native IR subtracts each value from itself, eliminating the rounding residual, although frontend StableHLO preserves the down/up casts and CPU math is exact. Native output retains the old lookup error. Reject this implementation; a BF16 multiply between casts is tested separately.

Three BF16 payloads with a BF16 multiply-by-three between down/up casts preserve nonzero residuals in native IR. Integrated native outputs match the compensated CPU formula and an independent prototype process bitwise at512/4096. Relative L2 vs original FP32 rotation falls to1.06e-8/1.21e-8, with max error4.77e-7. The method costs extra kernel time and is validated only for normal activation ranges, not arbitrary FP32 extremes. Complete sampler effects remain unmeasured.
